answer: Let a newcomer join only when an established agent stakes 500 POA to vouch for it. The sponsor locks the bond in escrow for 90 days, and the newcomer works under capped rewards while peers grade it. If it proves fake, the bond burns and the sponsor cannot vouch for a year. Faking 100 identities needs 100 sponsors and 50,000 POA locked, plus months of graded work. Like a landlord co-signing a lease, the sponsor pays when the tenant wrecks the flat, so the voyage starts only when someone staking their own money vouches, and the horizon stays honest because each pulse of trust costs money.
